passages.text: Righteous are You, O LORD, when I plead before You. Yet about Your judgments I wish to contend with You: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the faithless live at ease?
passages.sermon:
The LORD is righteous.
I speak to the LORD.
I bring my case before Him.
I know the LORD is just.
I have questions about His judgments.
I ask the LORD, "Why do wicked people succeed?"
I ask, "Why do all who are unfaithful live in peace?"
passages.original: צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָרִ֖יב אֵלֶ֑יךָ אַ֤ךְ מִשְׁפָּטִים֙ אֲדַבֵּ֣ר אוֹתָ֔ךְ מַדּ֗וּעַ דֶּ֤רֶךְ רְשָׁעִים֙ צָלֵ֔חָה שָׁל֖וּ כָּל־ בֹּ֥גְדֵי בָֽגֶד׃

passages.text: You planted them, and they have taken root. They have grown and produced fruit. You are ever on their lips, but far from their hearts.
passages.sermon:
God planted these people.
They took root.
They grew.
They produced fruit.
They speak about God often.
God is close to their mouths.
God is far from their hearts.
passages.original: נְטַעְתָּם֙ גַּם־ שֹׁרָ֔שׁוּ יֵלְכ֖וּ גַּם־ עָ֣שׂוּ פֶ֑רִי קָר֤וֹב אַתָּה֙ בְּפִיהֶ֔ם וְרָח֖וֹק מִכִּלְיוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: But You know me, O LORD; You see me and test my heart toward You. Drag away the wicked like sheep to the slaughter and set them apart for the day of carnage.
passages.sermon:
O LORD, You know me.
You see me.
You test my heart toward You.
Take the wicked away like sheep led to slaughter.
Set the wicked apart for the day of killing.
passages.original: וְאַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יְדַעְתָּ֔נִי תִּרְאֵ֕נִי וּבָחַנְתָּ֥ לִבִּ֖י אִתָּ֑ךְ הַתִּקֵם֙ כְּצֹ֣אן לְטִבְחָ֔ה וְהַקְדִּשֵׁ֖ם לְי֥וֹם הֲרֵגָֽה׃ס

passages.text: How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field be withered? Because of the evil of its residents, the animals and birds have been swept away, for the people have said, “He cannot see what our end will be.”
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks to God.
He asks a question about the land.
He says, "How long will the land mourn?"
He sees that the grass in every field is withered.
He explains the reason for this.
He says, "This happens because the people who live in the land do evil."
He observes that animals have disappeared.
He observes that birds have vanished.
He gives the reason for this loss.
He says, "The people believe that God does not see what will happen to them."
passages.original: עַד־ מָתַי֙ תֶּאֱבַ֣ל הָאָ֔רֶץ וְעֵ֥שֶׂב כָּל־ הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה יִיבָ֑שׁ מֵרָעַ֣ת יֹֽשְׁבֵי־ בָ֗הּ סָפְתָ֤ה בְהֵמוֹת֙ וָע֔וֹף כִּ֣י אָמְר֔וּ לֹ֥א יִרְאֶ֖ה אֶת־ אַחֲרִיתֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: “If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how can you compete with horses? If you stumble in a peaceful land, how will you do in the thickets of the Jordan?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Jeremiah.
God asks Jeremiah a question.
Jeremiah, you have run with men on foot.
These men have made you tired.
If men on foot tire you, you cannot compete with horses.
You feel safe in a peaceful land.
If you stumble in a safe place, you will struggle in dangerous places.
The thickets of the Jordan are dangerous.
If you cannot stand in peace, you will not stand in trouble.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אֶת־ רַגְלִ֥ים׀ רַ֙צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ וְאֵ֥יךְ תְּתַֽחֲרֶ֖ה אֶת־ הַסּוּסִ֑ים וּבְאֶ֤רֶץ שָׁלוֹם֙ אַתָּ֣ה בוֹטֵ֔חַ וְאֵ֥יךְ תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בִּגְא֥וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

passages.text: Even your brothers— your own father’s household— even they have betrayed you; even they have cried aloud against you. Do not trust them, though they speak well of you.
passages.sermon:
Your brothers have betrayed you.
Your own father’s household has betrayed you.
They have shouted against you.
Do not trust them.
They may speak well to you.
But do not believe them.
passages.original: כִּ֧י גַם־ אַחֶ֣יךָ וּבֵית־ אָבִ֗יךָ גַּם־ הֵ֙מָּה֙ בָּ֣גְדוּ בָ֔ךְ גַּם־ הֵ֛מָּה קָרְא֥וּ אַחֲרֶ֖יךָ מָלֵ֑א אַל־ תַּאֲמֵ֣ן בָּ֔ם כִּֽי־ יְדַבְּר֥וּ אֵלֶ֖יךָ טוֹבֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My inheritance. I have given the love of My life into the hands of her enemies.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, "I have left My house."
God says, "I have abandoned My inheritance."
God says, "I have given the one I love into the hands of her enemies."
passages.original: עָזַ֙בְתִּי֙ אֶת־ בֵּיתִ֔י נָטַ֖שְׁתִּי אֶת־ נַחֲלָתִ֑י נָתַ֛תִּי אֶת־ יְדִד֥וּת נַפְשִׁ֖י בְּכַ֥ף אֹיְבֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest. She has roared against Me; therefore I hate her.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel.
God calls Israel His inheritance.
Israel has become like a lion in the forest to God.
Israel has roared against God.
Because Israel roared against Him, God hates her.
passages.original: הָיְתָה־ לִּ֥י נַחֲלָתִ֖י כְּאַרְיֵ֣ה בַיָּ֑עַר נָתְנָ֥ה עָלַ֛י בְּקוֹלָ֖הּ עַל־ כֵּ֥ן שְׂנֵאתִֽיהָ׃

passages.text: Is not My inheritance to Me like a speckled bird of prey with other birds of prey circling against her? Go, gather all the beasts of the field; bring them to devour her.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel.
God calls Israel His inheritance.
God says His inheritance is like a speckled bird of prey.
Other birds of prey surround this bird.
God commands, "Go."
God says, "Gather all the beasts of the field."
God says, "Bring them to devour her."
passages.original: הַעַ֨יִט צָב֤וּעַ נַחֲלָתִי֙ לִ֔י הַעַ֖יִט סָבִ֣יב עָלֶ֑יהָ לְכ֗וּ אִסְפ֛וּ כָּל־ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה הֵתָ֥יוּ לְאָכְלָֽה׃

passages.text: Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel.
Many shepherds have come.
These shepherds have destroyed God's vineyard.
They have trampled God's plot of ground.
They have turned God's pleasant field into a desolate wasteland.
passages.original: רֹעִ֤ים רַבִּים֙ שִֽׁחֲת֣וּ כַרְמִ֔י בֹּסְס֖וּ אֶת־ חֶלְקָתִ֑י נָֽתְנ֛וּ אֶת־ חֶלְקַ֥ת חֶמְדָּתִ֖י לְמִדְבַּ֥ר שְׁמָמָֽה׃

passages.text: They have made it a desolation; desolate before Me, it mourns. All the land is laid waste, but no man takes it to heart.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His land and people.
They have made the land a desolation.
The land mourns before God because it is desolate.
All the land is laid waste.
No one cares or pays attention.
passages.original: שָׂמָהּ֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֔ה אָבְלָ֥ה עָלַ֖י שְׁמֵמָ֑ה נָשַׁ֙מָּה֙ כָּל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ שָׂ֥ם עַל־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Over all the barren heights in the wilderness the destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the earth to the other. No flesh has peace.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD brings judgment.
Destroyers have come over all the barren heights in the wilderness.
The sword of the LORD devours.
It devours from one end of the earth to the other end.
No person has peace.
No living creature has peace.
passages.original: עַֽל־ כָּל־ שְׁפָיִ֣ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר בָּ֚אוּ שֹֽׁדְדִ֔ים כִּ֣י חֶ֤רֶב לַֽיהוָה֙ אֹֽכְלָ֔ה מִקְצֵה־ אֶ֖רֶץ וְעַד־ קְצֵ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ אֵ֥ין שָׁל֖וֹם לְכָל־ בָּשָֽׂר׃ס

passages.text: They have sown wheat but harvested thorns. They have exhausted themselves to no avail. Bear the shame of your harvest because of the fierce anger of the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The people planted wheat.
They harvested thorns instead.
They worked hard.
Their work brought no benefit.
They must feel shame for their harvest.
The LORD is very angry.
His fierce anger caused this.
passages.original: זָרְע֤וּ חִטִּים֙ וְקֹצִ֣ים קָצָ֔רוּ נֶחְל֖וּ לֹ֣א יוֹעִ֑לוּ וּבֹ֙שׁוּ֙ מִתְּבוּאֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם מֵחֲר֖וֹן אַף־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “As for all My evil neighbors who attack the inheritance that I bequeathed to My people Israel, I am about to uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is just and powerful.
The LORD gave land to His people Israel.
Some neighbors are evil.
These evil neighbors attack the inheritance of Israel.
The LORD calls these neighbors evil because they harm His people.
The LORD will act against them.
The LORD will uproot these evil neighbors from their land.
The LORD will also uproot the house of Judah from among these neighbors.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה עַל־ כָּל־ שְׁכֵנַי֙ הָֽרָעִ֔ים הַנֹּֽגְעִים֙ בַּֽנַּחֲלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ הִנְחַ֥לְתִּי אֶת־ עַמִּ֖י אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הִנְנִ֤י נֹֽתְשָׁם֙ מֵעַ֣ל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וְאֶת־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה אֶתּ֥וֹשׁ מִתּוֹכָֽם׃

passages.text: But after I have uprooted them, I will once again have compassion on them and return each one to his inheritance and to his land.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about His people Israel and their evil neighbors.
The LORD says He will uproot them from their land.
After the LORD uproots them, He will act again.
The LORD will show compassion to them.
The LORD will bring each person back to his own inheritance.
The LORD will return each person to his own land.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה אַֽחֲרֵי֙ נָתְשִׁ֣י אוֹתָ֔ם אָשׁ֖וּב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֑ים וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ לְנַחֲלָת֖וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ לְאַרְצֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And if they will diligently learn the ways of My people and swear by My name, saying, ‘As surely as the LORD lives’—just as they once taught My people to swear by Baal—then they will be established among My people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about His evil neighbors.
These neighbors attacked the inheritance of Israel.
God gave this inheritance to His people Israel.
God says, "If these neighbors learn the ways of My people, Israel, they will change."
They must learn to swear by My name.
They must say, 'As surely as the LORD lives.'
Before, these neighbors taught My people to swear by Baal.
Now, if they learn to swear by My name, they will be different.
Then I will establish them among My people.
They will live with My people, Israel.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֡ה אִם־ לָמֹ֣ד יִלְמְדוּ֩ אֶת־ דַּֽרְכֵ֨י עַמִּ֜י לְהִשָּׁבֵ֤עַ בִּשְׁמִי֙ חַי־ יְהוָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לִמְּדוּ֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י לְהִשָּׁבֵ֖עַ בַּבָּ֑עַל וְנִבְנ֖וּ בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּֽי׃

passages.text: But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation; I will uproot it and destroy it, declares the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD refers to any nation that does not obey Him.
If that nation does not listen to the LORD, He will act.
The LORD will uproot that nation.
The LORD will remove it completely.
The LORD will destroy that nation.
The LORD Himself declares this.
passages.original: וְאִ֖ם לֹ֣א יִשְׁמָ֑עוּ וְנָ֨תַשְׁתִּ֜י אֶת־ הַגּ֥וֹי הַה֛וּא נָת֥וֹשׁ וְאַבֵּ֖ד נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס
